incidents.victim: Cyprus airline, telecom providers, and government/critical-infrastructure entities
incidents.vector: Phishing using fake AI-generated recruiter personas and resumes to deliver the KuboShell backdoor via an IPFS-based command-and-control channel.
incidents.impact: Intelligence gathering on government, infrastructure, and regional relationships; campaign reported expanding to target Saudi Arabian healthcare organizations.

incidents.victim: Chile Ministry of Foreign Affairs (visa-issuing system)
incidents.vector: Phishing email opened by a staff member in October led to compromise of the visa-issuing system.
incidents.impact: Visa-issuing system compromised; suspected use for sale of visas and fake identities. Authorities left the system running to avoid stranding travelers while investigating.

incidents.vector: Unspecified cybersecurity breach, details not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Stock trading halted on the Australian Securities Exchange pending disclosure.

incidents.vector: Breach of the Rackspace Spot platform's infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Customer account credentials stolen; Rackspace announced it is retiring the Spot service on December 8 as a result.

incidents.vector: Breach of a shared IT provider serving Flemish municipalities.
incidents.impact: Personal data of roughly 1.2 million residents stolen and offered for sale online.

incidents.vector: A compromised employee GitHub account was used to push unauthorized code into backend systems.
incidents.impact: Usernames, email addresses, and account metadata were stolen; 1Password states password vaults and secret keys were not accessed.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a limited subset of FinCEN systems, including the Bank Secrecy Act E-Filing portal.
incidents.impact: Some systems were taken offline and filing deadlines extended; no evidence the beneficial-ownership database was breached. FBI and CISA are investigating.

incidents.vector: Cybersecurity incident affecting administrative IT systems.
incidents.impact: Administrative systems affected; crude oil transport operations were not disrupted.

incidents.victim: Enterprises and developers using NuGet packages
incidents.vector: 13 malicious NuGet packages disguised as fake recruitment coding-assessment take-home tests, which side-loaded a malicious DLL via a legitimate Windows binary.
incidents.impact: An infostealer harvested browser credentials and sessions, giving attackers remote access to developer machines holding source code, SSH keys, and cloud tokens.

incidents.victim: Giorgia Linardi, spokesperson for Sea-Watch (migrant rescue NGO)
incidents.vector: Mobile phone infected with commercial-grade spyware.
incidents.impact: Nearly two months of covert surveillance of an NGO spokesperson; the case has been reported to prosecutors in Rome.

incidents.victim: CIA, National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, and Office of the Director of National Intelligence
incidents.vector: Attackers reportedly used an AI-driven offensive security framework to compromise an unclassified open-source-intelligence analysis system.
incidents.impact: Unclassified OSINT data was exposed, revealing analyst search priorities; classified networks were not affected.

incidents.victim: Santos Port Authority (Port of Santos, Brazil)
incidents.vector: Ransomware, likely delivered via malicious email or a compromised website.
incidents.impact: ERP and customer-facing systems were disrupted and some data lost after October 31; systems were fully restored on November 24.

incidents.vector: Valid stolen credentials were used to access production systems.
incidents.impact: Email addresses and password hashes were stolen for roughly 6% of users.

incidents.vector: An internal API was accidentally exposed to the internet and scraped.
incidents.impact: Customer contact details and some cloud log-storage credentials were exposed; affected clients were told to rotate credentials.

incidents.victim: LALIGA (Spanish football league) and an affiliated amateur-club platform
incidents.vector: Breach of a technology platform serving amateur football clubs affiliated with LALIGA.
incidents.impact: Personal data of fans was stolen across LALIGA and affiliated Spanish clubs.

incidents.victim: Unnamed Chinese identity-verification and data-lookup service
incidents.vector: A misconfigured, internet-exposed Elasticsearch database was left open.
incidents.impact: 1.6 billion records were exposed, including names, national IDs, phone numbers, and school/business registrations, covering more than 840 million individuals.

incidents.victim: Telecom carriers across Asia and their subscribers
incidents.vector: Backdoors planted in telecom infrastructure exploiting SS7 and Diameter signaling protocols.
incidents.impact: Location tracking and call/SMS interception of selected targets; the campaign has been active for more than two years.

incidents.vector: Two compromised hospital email accounts were used to send mass phishing emails to employees.
incidents.impact: Attackers threaten to publish medical records, prescriptions, lab results, and financial documents; scope is under investigation and patient care has not been disrupted.

incidents.vector: Unspecified cyberattack against institute systems.
incidents.impact: Personal information was compromised and two institute websites were disrupted; the intrusion has since been stopped.

incidents.victim: Roughly 700 French retail stores (supermarkets, butchers, food factories, a slaughterhouse)
incidents.vector: Hack of commercial refrigeration and freezer control systems on October 15, 2026; French authorities attributed the attack to an IRGC cyber unit on November 24.
incidents.impact: Freezers were disabled across hundreds of stores, causing tens of millions of euros in losses.

incidents.vector: A zero-day untrusted-deserialization vulnerability was used to take over six backend servers.
incidents.impact: No unauthorized package modifications were found; possible user data exposure could not be ruled out since reads were unlogged. All credentials were rotated.

incidents.vector: Unspecified security breach under investigation.
incidents.impact: The app, used for digital driver's licenses and state document filing, was taken offline pending investigation.

incidents.vector: Unspecified breach of customer-facing systems.
incidents.impact: Customer data was stolen.

incidents.victim: 18 EU politicians and law-enforcement officials, plus journalists
incidents.vector: Doxxing — public release of officials' and journalists' personal information.
incidents.impact: Personal data of officials (including Italy's foreign minister, Eurojust's president, Europol's cybercrime chief, and Germany's federal police chief) and journalists investigating Russian hacking and influence operations was published publicly.

incidents.victim: Roughly 80 major US newspapers (Boston Herald, Denver Post, Newsday, NY Daily News, and others)
incidents.vector: A card-skimming script was hidden in a shared third-party payment widget and exfiltrated stolen data via WebRTC.
incidents.impact: Payment card data was stolen from subscription payment pages across roughly 80 news sites over a nine-day period, affecting an estimated 15,000 page loads per day.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack over the weekend of November 21-22.
incidents.impact: The agency's energy certification platform was suspended.

incidents.victim: NetBeat (German web hosting provider) and its customers
incidents.vector: Unspecified breach of hosting infrastructure.
incidents.impact: All customer passwords were reset to evict the attacker from customer systems.

incidents.victim: WP connect (WordPress plugin developer) and downstream sites
incidents.vector: Compromise of the plugin developer's infrastructure, which added malware to six WordPress plugins.
incidents.impact: A backdoor was live for several hours; the malicious code has been removed from the plugins, but affected site owners must manually clean up infected sites.

incidents.vector: Suspected ransomware, possibly introduced via a previously compromised IT supplier, which encrypted hospital databases.
incidents.impact: Surgeries were postponed, cancer radiation therapy suspended, and chemotherapy sessions canceled; the hospital reverted to paper records.

incidents.vector: Breach of the online broker's customer support system.
incidents.impact: Personal data (names, addresses, ID scans) of more than 8,000 clients was stolen.

incidents.vector: Breach of FIFA's Microsoft cloud environment by a criminal extortion group.
incidents.impact: 12GB of personal and business data, including immigration documents and financial and legal records, was stolen; the extortion attempt failed and the data was published on a criminal forum.

incidents.victim: Undisclosed organizations running VMware vCenter and BeyondTrust Remote Support
incidents.vector: Exploited a zero-day in BeyondTrust Remote Support and a VMware vCenter authentication-bypass flaw (CVE-2026-123890) to move laterally and compromise vCenter infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Attacker gained administrator-level access to vCenter environments, deployed custom webshells and backdoors, and exfiltrated directory data; Mandiant/GTIG assess the group has deep platform expertise and significant resourcing.

incidents.victim: Two unnamed US-based organizations (government officials, defense contractors, NGOs)
incidents.vector: Compromised a cloud Super Admin account via a residential-proxy network and MFA push-notification fatigue, then reused stolen contacts and pretexts to phish a second organization through federated Entra ID single sign-on.
incidents.impact: Mass exfiltration of emails, cloud drive files, and employee directories from both organizations; the attacker retained persistent access for months using rogue MFA devices and passkeys, and new phishing activity tied to the group was observed as recently as November 2026.

incidents.victim: Organizations using the Microsoft Agent Framework Python package
incidents.vector: Two unauthorized versions (1.26.1, 1.26.2) of the agent-framework Python package were uploaded to PyPI containing credential-stealing code.
incidents.impact: Any environment that installed the malicious versions had cloud, CI/CD, and Git credentials exposed; Microsoft pulled the packages, took the GitHub repository offline, and urged full credential rotation for affected environments.

incidents.victim: 178+ organizations using Optimizely Web Experimentation, including major media, technology, and financial services brands
incidents.industry: Media / Technology / Financial services (multi-sector via SaaS supply chain)
incidents.vector: Exploited a vulnerability (CVE-2026-132224) in Optimizely's account registration flow to inject malicious JavaScript, served to visitors from the vendor's own legitimate CDN and certificate.
incidents.impact: Malicious code swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses, skimmed payment card data, and attempted to deliver mobile exploit kits to iOS visitors across 178+ sites; roughly $7,500 in cryptocurrency was stolen before Optimizely patched the flaw and removed the code.

incidents.vector: A forgotten cloud access key issued to a third-party AI service provider was abused, after which the attacker deployed an AI-driven offensive framework for lateral movement.
incidents.impact: Attacker had nearly two days of access to Barracuda's cloud environment and internal network.

incidents.vector: Unspecified breach of payment processing systems.
incidents.impact: Payment card data was stolen; affected customers were notified to monitor for fraud.

incidents.vector: Breach exposing application code, databases, and API/integration keys.
incidents.impact: The company fully replaced its cloud environment and expects a $2.5 million loss as a result of the incident.
